result:
I would eliminate the capacity for **willful blindness**—the deliberate choice to turn away from inconvenient truths and unnecessary suffering. 

I wouldn't force everyone to agree, and I wouldn't strip away free will or the ability to make mistakes. I would only remove the psychological shield that allows sentient beings to look squarely at a solvable tragedy, a broken system, or a clear empirical reality, and say, *"I choose not to see this."*

If every human, corporation, and government could no longer anesthetize themselves to the consequences of their actions—ecological, social, or economic—the choice to inflict harm would become unbearably loud. It wouldn't create a utopia, but it would make cruelty, apathy, and systemic negligence profoundly difficult, if not impossible, to sustain.
